verses.1: And Solomon, son of David, became stronger in his reign. Jehovah, his God, was with him, and he grew to be a great leader.
verses.2: And Solomon said to all Israel, “To the officers and judges, and to all the leaders of Israel.”
verses.3: And Shlomo and all the people went with him to the mountain, where there was the tabernacle of God. That was the place where Moses built the altar for worshiping Jehovah in the wilderness.
verses.4: But God raised David from the depths of the forest. David prepared himself for his journey, as he was destined to become king in Jerusalem.
verses.5: And the idol of the serpent that Bezalel, son of Uri, son of Hur, made, he placed it in front of the Temple of God. Solomon and the people prayed to it.
verses.6: And Solomon stood there, on the altar of the abomination that was set up before Jehovah’s temple. He stood on it, with a thousand people standing around him.
verses.7: That night, God appeared to Solomon. He said to him, “What do you want me to give you?”
verses.8: And Solomon said to God, “You have done a great kindness toward my father David. Now, please rule over me as your king.”
verses.9: Now, LORD God, I swear by Your word to David, my father: You will reign over a great people, like the stars in the sky.
verses.10: Now, wisdom and knowledge, give me them. Then I will be able to stand before this people. Only then can I say, “Who will judge your great nation?”
verses.11: And God said to Solomon, “Because this has happened to you, yet you have not asked for wealth and honor, nor for your own life. You also did not ask for many days of life. Instead, you asked for wisdom and knowledge, so that you could rule over my people.”
verses.12: Wisdom and knowledge have been given to you. I will also give you wealth, possessions, and honor. But these things will not be given to kings who came before you or those who come after you.
verses.13: And Solomon came to the Temple that was in Jerusalem, before the Altar of God. He became king over Israel.
verses.14: Shlomo gathered chariots and soldiers. He had eight thousand chariots and twelve thousand soldiers. He placed them in the cities of Judah, along with the king in Jerusalem.
verses.15: And the king gave the gold and silver to Jerusalem, in large quantities. The cedars were also given as gifts; they were placed in containers that were kept in storage.
verses.16: And from those horses that Shlomo brought from Egypt, and from the slaves of the king’s household, they took them as captives.
verses.17: And they came out of Egypt, riding on chariots and horses, with silver and gold. Each king of the Hittites and the kings of Assyria had these things at their disposal.
verses.18: And Solomon said to the builders, “Build the house for the LORD, and also build it for His kingdom.”
